entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.1.1
entry.content:
Fixes

  • The island no longer crashes inside Windows' media controls while media apps or a browser's videos (like YouTube in Chrome) keep changing: a media session that goes away (or stops being the one shown) is kept with its handlers for 10 seconds before the media thread lets it go, since Windows may still be calling it on its own threads (also when the media thread stops, without keeping the island waiting). If the island's process ever crashes (an NTSTATUS exit code), the explorer part starts it again, at most 3 times in 10 minutes, and only when it was Windhawk's own windhawk.exe at Explorer's integrity level (decided at its hello, while it runs), launched with CreateProcessInternalW like the tool mod snippet. On Windhawk 2.0 the island runs in windhawk-mod.exe, which Windhawk starts itself, so the mod doesn't start it again there.
  • With the Fixed style's notches minimized, a notification's app icon peeks out only of the notch with the bell, not out of every notch, and no longer for the app you're using (a taskbar badge from the app in front).
  • A click on a notification opens its app when the app's own notification handler doesn't answer (its COM activation fails within 5 seconds), instead of doing nothing: the island falls back to the app's window, its tray icon or the app itself.
  • An app's own counter on its taskbar button (like WhatsApp's) no longer keeps its icon on the island as a waiting notification while the list is empty ("No notifications", so no "Clear all" to dismiss it): it counts as seen when the app comes to the front (or is in front when it changes) or its icon on the island is clicked, and shows again when the counter goes away and comes back or its number grows.
  • Sleep in the power button's menu no longer hibernates PCs with Modern Standby: with no S1-S3, it turns the screen off like Start > Sleep instead of calling SetSuspendState.
  • QQ's and WeChat's message preview shows again when hovering their icon in the taskbar's tray with tray icons on the island: the island answers Shell_NotifyIconGetRect with its own place only while the mouse is on that icon on the island (#7157).
  • The settings window takes much less of the processor in its first seconds: the preview's hint, the "+ Line" glow and the other hints that only fade or pulse draw at most 30 times a second instead of at the monitor's rate.
  • Dock: games' icons (like Steam's) and other apps without an icon of their own in the Start menu no longer go empty when Windows' icon cache is out of date (an empty picture now counts as none and the next source is tried), nor show a small icon magnified: the last fallback reads the window's program's icon from the file as big as the dock shows it, before the window's own 32 px icon (#7207).
  • Right after a Windows update whose taskbar.dll symbols Microsoft hasn't published yet (KB5132061, taskbar.dll 10.0.26100.9974, was 🔴 on the symbol cache's status page), the explorer part no longer stops as a whole. ExplorerModInit returned FALSE when HookTaskbarDllSymbols failed, so the island lost its tray icons too, which need no symbols (subclass and WM_COPYDATA). Now the taskbar stays as Windows draws it (g_taskbarSymbols false: no symbol hook is set, and GetTaskbarXamlRoot/GetSecondaryTaskbarXamlRoot return null instead of calling a symbol pointer), ApplyToTaskbar counts the main taskbar as ready so the late start goes on, and the tray icons and the apps asking for attention keep reaching the island. The explorer part keeps the taskbar.dll version without symbols in the mod's storage (taskbarNoSymbols, cleared once they load), and the main island shows a sticky notice saying why, once per version and only when the chosen taskbar needs them (the dock, the transparent taskbar, only the apps, or the tray hidden). Its "Details" button, or a click on it, opens the island's What's new, where this fix tells why (the whole text may not fit a smaller notice). The dock comes back once the symbols are published and load with Explorer (its next start). Without taskbar.dll at all, it still returns FALSE.
  • The islands no longer stall every few seconds on PCs with apps chosen for the visualizer (since 3.1). Each island, every 3 s, read all the default output's audio sessions again once per chosen app, each read making a new IAudioSessionManager2, asking for every session's state and process and opening each program (~12 ms a read), all on the islands' thread: with 8 apps on 3 islands a tick took 30 ms to over a second, found with a per-message timing log and by sampling the thread. Now one list (g_audioSessions) is read at most every 1.5 s for every island and app, the output's session manager is kept (made again for another default output or after a failure), each program's file is looked up once per process, and the list is released with the islands, before CoUninitialize.

entry.title: Auto-Pause on Disconnect 1.0.0
entry.content:
Auto-Pause on Disconnect

Pauses what you were listening to when the headphones go away: the 3.5 mm cable pulled out, a Bluetooth headset dropped, a USB DAC unplugged. The action lands after Windows has moved the sound back to the built-in speakers, so there is no one-second blast through them.

It does not have to be a pause. The action is a setting, and so is whether it runs on a disconnect, on a connect, or both.

Features

  • Watches the default output device, so wired, Bluetooth and USB removals are caught the same way.
  • Toggle play/pause, mute the output, or unmute it.
  • Waits 300 ms by default before acting, which is enough for Windows to finish moving the stream. Adjustable.
  • Repeats inside one second are folded into a single action. One unplug raises several notifications, and play/pause is a toggle.
  • Only acts while an app is actually playing by default, so it never starts playback on its own.
  • Switching the output by hand is left alone; the old device has to be gone for the action to run.

Settings

  • When a device disconnects and When a device connects pick the direction. Connects are off by default, because plugging headphones in moves the default output too.
  • Audio role to watch is Multimedia by default, or Console, or Both.
  • Action is Toggle play/pause, Mute the default output, or Unmute it.
  • Delay before acting (ms) is how long Windows gets before the action runs, 0 to 3000.
  • Ignore repeats within (ms) is the window used to fold the burst, 0 to 5000.
  • Act only while audio is playing keeps the toggle from starting playback.

Good to know

Play/pause is a toggle, not a pause: if playback was already stopped, it starts again. Leaving Act only while audio is playing on keeps it honest, and the Windows disconnect sound is not counted as playback.

The mute action applies to whichever device is the default after the switch, which is normally the internal speakers. Pair When a device connects with unmute if the headset should bring the sound back when it returns.

The mod runs in a small process of its own rather than inside Explorer, and uses the Windows Core Audio API. The notification callback only wakes a worker thread; the delay, the playback check and the media key all happen there.

entry.title: Explorer Fast Navigation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Fast Navigation

Makes folder navigation faster and less visually disruptive in File Explorer by removing intermediate redraw flicker and deferring toolbar updates until folder contents are loaded.

How it works

In Windows 10 and Windows 11, switching folders triggers intermediate window clearing ("Working on it..." placeholder) and multiple synchronous redraw events from the Ribbon and XAML command bar before files are enumerated.

This mod optimizes the navigation pipeline:

  • Redraw suppression: Suppresses intermediate window clears and synchronous redraw flushes during folder transitions.
  • Deferred toolbar updates: Defers Ribbon and XAML command bar state notifications while files are being enumerated, flushing them once file enumeration completes (DISPID_FILELISTENUMDONE) or batch processing settles.
  • UI freeze reduction: Prevents the UI thread from locking up during folder switches and column grouping changes, lowering CPU repaint spikes.
  • Safety fallback: Incorporates a configurable safety ceiling to ensure pending UI updates always flush even on slow network drives or non-responsive storage.

Observed results

Real-world behavior varies depending on the storage medium and system load:

  • High-speed NVMe drives: Windows virtualizes viewports quickly, but the mod noticeably removes the transient white flicker, suppresses UI repaint churn, and keeps window headers responsive.
  • Mechanical hard drives and laptops: On rotational HDDs or resource-constrained mobile CPUs where disk seek times and background file enumeration can cause visible stalls, the mod eliminates the intermediate "Working on it..." freeze and keeps the Explorer interface smooth during heavy folder browsing and column grouping operations.

Settings

  • Defer immediate navigation paints: Defer immediate activation and layout paints while Explorer switches views.
  • Defer classic ribbon updates: Delay classic ribbon refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer XAML command bar updates: Delay modern command bar refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer navigation bar updates: Delay navigation state updates in classic and modern navigation bars.
  • Safety fallback ceiling (ms): Maximum time (in ms) to wait before forcing a deferred UI update to flush if navigation stalls or on slow storage.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 (21H2, 22H2, 23H2, 24H2)
  • Windows 10 (1809 and later)
  • Architectures: 64-bit (x86-64, ARM64)

Support

If you find this mod useful, you can support its development and maintenance:

  • Support on Buy Me a Coffee

Credits

  • Based on the original implementation by Vivy (@VivyVCCS / enginelesscc).
  • Modernized, refactored, and maintained by gilnett.

entry.title: Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router 2.6.1
entry.content:
🔊 Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router

Volume control for games and setups with several output devices, on Windows 11 and 10: hotkeys for the focused game or app, per-app audio routing, volume locks, Deafen and a replacement volume OSD. Its mixer popup opens on a hotkey on top of any window — including borderless and fullscreen games — without taking the keyboard focus, so games are never minimized. It runs in its own small Windhawk process, not inside Explorer.

✨ Highlights

  • Game hotkeys – change or mute the focused game/app on every device it plays to, without opening anything. UWP apps and protected/elevated games are recognized too.
  • Per-app audio routing – send any app to another output device with the ⇄ button or a right-click.
  • Volume lock – pin the volume of an app or device; a watchdog restores it when a game or Windows changes it. Locks are kept across restarts and marked with a padlock.
  • Deafen background (BETA) – one hotkey mutes or ducks everything except the focused app and your whitelist; pressing it again restores every app individually.
  • Custom volume OSD (BETA) – 9 styles, can replace the Windows volume flyout for the media keys and the volume tooltip of the taskbar, draggable. Like the Windows flyout, it stays while the pointer rests on it, and the mouse wheel or a click on its bar changes the volume.
  • Mixer popup – volume and mute of every app on every output device at once, with live VU meters (up to 60 FPS while open); 17 layouts and 22 color themes.
  • Correct scaling – interface scale 30–300 % multiplied by the Windows display scaling of each monitor; the popup shrinks automatically when it would not fit on the screen.
  • Light on resources – nothing is polled while the popup is closed: the OSD and the volume locks react to Windows audio events, and the keyboard and mouse hooks are installed only while a feature needs them.

🎛️ Mixer layouts

Modern Cards · Compact Strip · Hi-Fi Studio Meters · Fluent Flyout · Cyber Radial HUD · Studio Mixing Desk · Floating Minimal Pill · Cyberpunk Neon Grid · Retro Cassette · LED Meter Bridge · Arcade Panel · Broadcast Console (dual VU) · Control Center Pills · Frosted Glass Tiles · Retro Terminal · Soft Neumorphic · Vertical Channel Strips.

🎨 Themes

Windows 11 Mica · Modern Dark · Light Fluent · AMOLED Black · Frosted Glass · System Accent · Classic Blue · Dracula · Nordic Frost · Cyberpunk Neon · Retro Amber · Tokyo Night · Sunset · Catppuccin Mocha · Forest · Monochrome · Deep Ocean · Rosé Pine · Gruvbox · Solarized Dark · Matrix Green · Midnight Gold.

📺 OSD styles (BETA)

Windows 11 capsule · compact pill · detailed (name, level and device) · circular ring · vertical edge bar · frosted glass · tactical game HUD · stealth dot matrix · Control Center pill.

  • Once the pointer moves onto the OSD, it works like the Windows flyout and stays on screen until the pointer leaves. The mouse wheel or touchpad scrolling over it changes the volume it shows (the master volume or the app), a click or a drag on its bar sets the level, a click on its icon mutes, and a right-click closes it. Otherwise clicks pass through it (unless dragging is enabled), and a hidden pointer (games) is ignored.
  • Replace the Windows volume flyout: the media volume keys and the mouse wheel over the taskbar notification area (tray icons and clock) go through the mod, so Windows doesn't show its own flyout or the Windows 11 volume tooltip. Other volume changes, such as touchpad gestures, headset buttons or laptop hotkey drivers, are made by Windows itself; when Windows shows its flyout for one of them, the mod keeps that flyout invisible (it clips Explorer's indicator window to an empty region and hides it) and shows its own OSD, which follows every step, at 0 % and 100 % too. Only the very first flyout after Explorer starts can show for a moment, before the mod knows its window. Brightness and other Windows indicators use the same window and stay visible: Windows reports brightness changes, so the brightness indicator shows even at 0 % or 100 % volume, except when the brightness itself is already at its limit (then nothing changes and nothing is reported). Airplane mode and other rare indicators shown right after an outside volume change, or at 0 % or 100 %, can be hidden as well. While the option is on, other tray apps and mods that react to the wheel in the notification area (for example Taskbar Volume Control with the tray area as its scroll area) don't get it. Volume indicators of manufacturer utilities (laptop or keyboard software) are separate programs and aren't affected.

⌨️ Hotkeys

Action Default
Open / close mixer Win+Alt+V
Active app volume up / down not assigned
Active app mute / unmute not assigned
Deafen background (when enabled) not assigned
Master volume up / down / mute not assigned

Only the mixer hotkey is set by default, so the mod doesn't take shortcuts that other apps use.

Format: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win + one key (A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, Up, Down, Left, Right, Space, PageUp, PageDown, Num0–Num9, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, Mute…), joined with +. Leave a hotkey empty to disable it. On keyboard layouts with AltGr, Right Alt doesn't count as Ctrl+Alt.

🖱️ Using the mixer

  • Drag a slider or scroll over it to change the volume.
  • Click an app icon to mute or unmute it.
  • Click ⇄ (or right-click a row) to route the app to another device or to lock its volume.
  • Right-click or double-click a device header to make it the Windows default device.
  • Press any key or click outside to close the mixer.

🌐 Language

The mixer, menus and OSD use Language → Mod interface language (automatic, English, Ukrainian, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Russian). The settings page is translated into the same languages and follows the language of Windhawk itself (Windhawk → Settings → Language); other languages show English.

⚠️ Notes

  • Features marked BETA (OSD, Deafen background) are off by default. The mod adds no tray icon: the mixer opens with its hotkey.
  • "Route audio to" uses the same undocumented Windows API as the "App volume and device preferences" page of Windows and EarTrumpet; some apps only switch the device after their audio stream restarts.
  • While a game or app running as administrator is focused, hotkeys work through standard Windows hotkeys: holding volume up/down doesn't repeat there, and Ctrl+Alt combinations don't work there.

🧹 What stays after the mod is disabled

Like the Windows volume mixer, the mod changes Windows' own audio preferences, and Windows keeps them:

  • Output device of an app chosen with "Route audio to": stays until you pick "Windows default device" in the same menu, or use Settings → System → Sound → Volume mixer → Reset.
  • Default output device chosen in the mixer: stays, like a change made in the Windows sound settings.
  • Volume and mute levels of devices and apps: Windows remembers them, as with any mixer.
  • Deafen background: if the mod stops while Deafen is on (crash, shutdown, power loss), it restores the muted and ducked apps the next time it starts.
  • Volume locks are stored by the mod and are no longer enforced while it's disabled.
  • Windows volume flyout (with "Replace the Windows volume flyout"): the mod gives Explorer's indicator window back its normal shape when it's disabled. If its process is killed instead, the Windows flyout stays invisible until Explorer restarts (for example after signing out).

entry.title: Sleep Countdown Reset 1.0.0
entry.content:
Sleep Countdown Reset

Media servers such as Plex keep the PC awake while streaming, but idle time still accumulates. When playback ends and the request is released, Windows checks the expired idle time and sleeps immediately, leaving no time to start the next episode/media/exchange.

This mod hooks the keep-awake APIs inside each server process. Right before the server releases the request, the mod takes over with its own, for a configurable grace period or, by default, the active power plan's sleep timeout. After this period, if playback does not return, the PC sleeps normally.

Display timer and monitor state stay under Windows' control. While the grace period runs, powercfg /requests lists the mod's request under SYSTEM.

Supported servers

Included by default:

  • Plex Media Server
  • Emby Server (EmbyServer.exe)
  • Jellyfin (jellyfin.exe): only with the third-party Prevent Sleep plugin, since Jellyfin alone doesn't keep the PC awake. On PCs with Modern Standby the plugin switches power plans instead, which this mod can't see.

Can be added (see below):

  • Universal Media Server: javaw.exe, with its "Prevent sleep" option set to Playback. That process name is shared by every Java program, so they all get the grace period.
  • qBittorrent (qbittorrent.exe), with "Inhibit system sleep" enabled: grace period after downloads finish.

Not needed: remote desktop and game streaming hosts (Sunshine, Parsec, Steam Remote Play). They forward the remote keyboard and mouse as local input, so Windows already counts the user as present.

Not covered: Windows file sharing (SMB). It runs inside the kernel, with no process to hook.

Adding a program

  1. While the program is serving, run powercfg /requests in a terminal as administrator. The program must be listed under SYSTEM or EXECUTION.
  2. In Windhawk, open this mod's Advanced tab, add the executable name (e.g. qbittorrent.exe) to the custom process inclusion list, and save.
  3. With debug logging enabled, the log should show hooked SetThreadExecutionState for the new process. If the program runs as a Windows service and nothing shows up, check that Windhawk is allowed to inject into services.

Limitation

If the server process exits while holding the request, Windows drops it without any API call, and the mod can't see the release.

entry.title: Mutelith 1.0
entry.content:
Mutelith

Fixes Discord double audio when screen sharing on Windows setups that use virtual audio devices, where viewers hear the game or desktop audio twice, or hear their own microphone coming back with a delay.

Provider Target device (Discord muted)
SteelSeries Sonar SteelSeries Sonar - Microphone
FxSound FxSound Speakers

The provider is detected from the default output device.

While Discord is running, the mod:

  1. Mutes Discord on the provider's target device and on every device outside the provider (speakers, headphones). Only the mute changes, never the volume.
  2. Leaves the provider's other virtual devices alone.
  3. When the mod is disabled, or the default device switches to another provider, unmutes Discord on the devices the rule no longer covers.

With FxSound, FxSound Speakers is usually the only FxSound device, so every other output device is outside the provider and Discord is muted on all of them, voice chat included.

It reacts to Windows audio notifications right away (default device changed, device added or removed, new audio session such as a screen share, a muted session was unmuted) and also checks every 30 seconds.

Windows remembers the mute

The mute is Discord's per-app setting in the Volume Mixer, and Windows saves it for each output device, so it outlives the mod. The mod records each device it muted Discord on and unmutes Discord there once the rule no longer covers it, including after a crash. Windows only lets the mod do that while Discord is running and to have an audio session on that device. If Discord isn't listed for a device in the Volume Mixer when you disable the mod, Discord stays muted there: open the Volume Mixer and unmute Discord, or enable the mod again while Discord is playing audio on that device and switch the default device away from the provider. A mute you set yourself in the Volume Mixer is left alone.

Mutelith app

This is the same rule as the Mutelith app. Use one or the other: while Mutelith.exe is running, the mod does nothing.

Designed and tested for one virtual audio provider at a time.

entry.title: OSD Custom Pill 4.9.11
entry.content:
OSD Custom Pill

An animated on-screen indicator for volume, brightness and virtual desktops on Windows 11.

Volume and brightness

Shows an icon, a progress bar and the current value. The indicator expands when it appears and retracts when it closes.

Elastic deformation

Increasing a value moves and stretches the pill to the right; decreasing it moves the pill to the left. Repeated changes build up the deformation. When you release the key, the pill returns with a spring effect.

The movement, stretching, spring damping and return strength can be adjusted independently in the mod settings.

Compact mode

After several changes in a row, the indicator can become smaller to take up less space. You can choose how many changes activate this mode and when it returns to normal.

Size and position

Adjust the pill's width, height and distance from the bottom of the screen. Opening and closing delays can also be changed.

Virtual desktops

Displays the current virtual desktop name or number when switching desktops. This indicator has its own size, position, animation and duration settings.

Settings

All options are available in Windhawk's Settings tab, with translated labels in supported languages. The main groups are:

Appearance and position — dimensions and screen placement.

Opening and closing — delays and spring response.

Stretching and rebound — movement distance, deformation and elastic return.

Compact mode — activation threshold and return timing.

Virtual desktop indicator — label, dimensions, timing and animation.

Timing values are in milliseconds. Size values are based on 100% display scaling.

entry.title: Arabic Keyboard Layout Fixer 1.3.0
entry.content:
Arabic Keyboard Layout Fixer

Fixes the common frustration of typing Arabic text while the keyboard is accidentally set to English (or vice versa).

How to use:

  1. Select/highlight any mistyped text in any app (Notepad, Word, Browser, ERP, etc.).
  2. Press Alt + Z (or your custom configured hotkey).
  3. The text instantly flips to the correct language!

Features:

  • Bi-directional (AR <-> EN): Automatically detects language direction.
  • Smart Shift / Caps Lock fix: Resolves accidental Shift / Caps-Lock misfires.
  • Configurable hotkeys: Customize your hotkey from mod settings without conflicts.
  • Universal compatibility: Works in modern browsers, Office, and legacy Win32/ERP applications.
  • Dedicated tool process: Runs safely as an independent background tool mod.
  • Full clipboard preservation: Restores all clipboard formats (images, files, text) and keeps history clean.

entry.title: Explorer Translucent Menus 1.0.2
entry.content:
Explorer Translucent Menus

Apply translucent materials to classic Win32 popup menus in File Explorer. Windows continues to provide menu items, layout, commands, keyboard navigation, and shell extensions. Windows 11's modern context menu is left unchanged.

This is an Explorer-only, menu-focused alternative to the archived TranslucentFlyouts project. It covers classic popup menus hosted by explorer.exe, including desktop and File Explorer context menus. It leaves the main Explorer window background, ordinary controls, and other processes unchanged.

Screenshots

Materials in light and dark themes

Tint and transparency adjustments

Borders and submenus

Requirements

  • Windows 11 22H2 or later (build 22621+), 64-bit.
  • Desktop composition and Windows transparency effects enabled.
  • No other renderer modifying the same Explorer menus.

To open a classic context menu on Windows 11, select Show more options or use Shift+F10. Select Native to disable all hooks. For a temporary bypass, enable Hold Ctrl to bypass in the settings, then hold Ctrl before opening a menu.

Materials

Material Tint opacity
Native No modifications
Solid Always opaque
Transparent Adjustable, no blur
Acrylic Adjustable tint over blur
Modern Acrylic Adjustable tint color, fixed opacity
System Acrylic Fixed Windows recipe
Mica / Mica Alt Fixed Windows recipes

Tint opacity changes the material, not text or icons. Theme selection controls the light or dark palette. Hover highlight opacity can be adjusted separately. Unrecognized saved material values use Acrylic.

Appearance

Enable Hide menu border to suppress the outline on modified menus. This preserves menu dimensions and works with rounded or square corners. Native mode and Ctrl bypass retain the complete Windows appearance. The option also protects the outline setting from later Shell/UxTheme updates while the modified menu is being tracked.

Legacy icon repair converts copied RGB bitmaps to premultiplied alpha. Optional background removal clears only matching corner-connected white, black, or magenta regions. Disable background removal for icons with intentional borders. Transfers that declare per-pixel alpha, and bitmaps with ambiguous partial alpha, retain the original GDI behavior. The mod does not guess whether an existing alpha bitmap is straight or premultiplied.

Scope and rendering approach

This mod keeps the Shell's immersive owner-draw enabled and preserves native menu layout, commands, and shell extensions. Effects are scoped to supported classic popups while a menu is tracked. Preparation validates resources before applying effects and exposes the popup to drawing hooks only after commit. Only successful state changes are recorded for cleanup. Unassociated memory DCs are left to Windows; owner-draw memory DCs require an exact synchronous WM_DRAWITEM match. GDI and UxTheme hooks are installed in Explorer, but forward to Windows outside a tracked menu. The scope is the popup effect, rather than a replacement for Explorer's overall interface rendering.

Translucent Windows and Win32 UI Modernizer already offer translucent classic menus. Translucent Windows shares background-effect configuration between windows and flyouts, with menu drawing integrated into its broader theme-rendering path. Win32 UI Modernizer lets users disable its Explorer section and other general features, but its modern menu modes disable immersive owner-draw and also modernize ComboBox dropdowns.

The purpose of this separate implementation is to provide a dedicated popup renderer that retains the Shell's owner-draw path and can accompany a separate Explorer background renderer. Restricting process targets or adding material presets alone does not provide that rendering behavior. An equivalent mode in a broader UI mod would need to isolate menu rendering and preserve immersive owner-draw as well.

Compatibility

Menu effects from these mods conflict when enabled on the same Explorer popups:

  • Translucent Windows: Flyout effects also renders classic menus, dropdowns, and tooltips. Disable that option to remove its flyout effects.
  • Win32 UI Modernizer: set Menus and dropdowns to Native (no modernization). Both modern modes apply their own acrylic rendering and disable immersive owner-draw.

These settings turn off their direct menu features. Their remaining Explorer effects and shared drawing hooks depend on other settings, so compatibility must be evaluated with the configuration in use. To avoid their remaining hooks in Explorer while continuing to use them in other applications, exclude explorer.exe from their targets in Windhawk's Advanced tab.

This mod is also compatible with ExplorerBlurMica, which supplies the main Explorer window backdrop. This mod keeps its effects confined to classic popup menus and leaves the main window backdrop to ExplorerBlurMica.

Unknown owner-drawn menus, custom background brushes, high contrast, remote sessions, disabled transparency, and recognized conflicting renderers are left unchanged. Settings changes reload the mod. Menu opening animations follow the Windows settings and the caller's flags, including when effects are active.

Menus whose previous system-backdrop value cannot be read stay native. Unreadable optional dark-mode and corner preferences are left unchanged. Recorded values are restored on live-window cleanup; failed restores remain pending for retry. There are no public getters for prior blur regions or extended-frame margins, and the Accent getter is unavailable on some builds. Cleanup of those states is best-effort, not a lossless restoration guarantee for an unknown renderer. A missing border-color snapshot likewise uses the Windows default on cleanup. Destroyed popup HWNDs release their window-owned effects without extra resets.

The implementation uses version-dependent Windows interfaces: the composition attribute exports, UxTheme ordinal 74, the DarkMode::Menu theme, menu layout message 0x1e2, and Shell window properties. It does not read private Shell item structures, patch instructions, download symbols, or replace the menu loop.

Troubleshooting

Enable log output in Windhawk's Advanced tab to record menu preparation, material and border application results, native fallback reasons, and cleanup. There is no separate logging setting in this mod. Native mode registers no menu hooks, so it reports initialization rather than individual menu openings.

Credits and license

Informed by TranslucentFlyouts, Translucent Windows, and Custom Cached Context Menu. This implementation is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later.

entry.title: Outlook Refined 0.6.2
entry.content:
• Credit the author in the readme, with a link to their site.
  • Align the agenda and its divider with the favorites list above them. The agenda was positioned against the navigation pane while the list sits inside Outlook's own scrolling container, so the two halves of the pane never shared an edge.
  • Give the folder names back 18px. The element holding the folder tree reserves a scrollbar gutter while its own overflow is hidden, so nothing is ever drawn in it; releasing the reservation takes the pane from 163px of usable width to 181px on a 197px pane and leaves 8px on both sides.

entry.title: Taskbar Fluent Media Player 1.7.0
entry.content:
The big ones

  • Its own settings window. Right-click the player and pick Settings. It's built in the Windows 11 style with Mica, sorted into pages, and changes show on the player while you make them. It comes in 15 languages and follows your Windows language by default.
  • Settings live in the mod now. The first time 1.7 runs, it copies everything from Windhawk's settings page, so you don't lose anything. Save keeps your changes, and closing only warns you if something really differs from what's saved.
  • Move any part of the player. Album art, track info, buttons and the visualizer can each be detached and placed somewhere else on the taskbar or tray, with their own background and monitor.
  • Progress bar. It can sit under any part of the player or the whole thing, on its own line or drawn on top. Click or drag it to seek.
  • Vertical taskbars. If yours is docked left or right, the text and album art turn to read along it and the buttons stack up.
  • Monitor buttons. Pick a monitor by clicking its button, numbered like Windows. Click the selected one again to hide the player. Monitors that aren't connected stay gray and become available when you plug them in.

Visualizer

  • "Only listen to the app in the player", on by default, so a Discord call or a game won't move the bars (Windows 11). (#93, #85)
  • New: it can fill the background behind the whole player.
  • New: Line style, and a Micro version that fits next to the artist text. (#16)
  • Pick which audio device it listens to, including recording devices. (#17, #50)
  • Hide it when nothing is playing. (#14)
  • Tune each of the 7 frequency bands.

Player and layout

  • Set the order of album art, text, buttons and visualizer. (#32)
  • "Media player offset" moves the player without making the taskbar wider, which helps with floating Taskbar Styler themes. (#88)
  • Reorder the media buttons and right-click menu items.
  • Hide the whole player while paused, after a delay you choose. (#14)
  • Hide the Windows Widgets button.

Text

  • Show the album name instead of the artist, or only when there's no cover. (#38)
  • Custom text formats with %title%, %artist%, %album% and %artist_or_album%. (#38)
  • Show the playback time (like 2:02/4:24) instead of the artist.
  • Hide the text when nothing is playing.

Clicks and apps

  • Choose an app to open when you click the player with nothing playing. (#23)
  • New click actions: minimize, open or minimize, and close the media app. (#53)
  • "Only show these apps" mode, and the app filter moved out of Debug into Behaviour. (#64)

Mini player

  • Seek bar, with its own color. (#62)
  • Background options: Acrylic, solid color, album colors gradient or blurred cover. (#48)
  • Corner radius setting, and the bottom icon row can be turned off. (#84)

Settings window extras

  • Choose the window's background: Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic or Acrylic Thin. Acrylic shows what's behind the window, so it works with live wallpapers that Mica can't see, and has its own transparency and blur sliders.
  • The title bar can match the window, stay as Windows draws it, or take any color.
  • The page fades at its top and bottom edges while you scroll.
  • Any color can follow the album, including the window's own accent, which fades to the new color when the song changes.
  • Report a bug from inside the window. You choose whether to attach errors, crash info, the log and your settings. Reports also include your PC name and Windows user name, and the form says so.
  • Reset to Windhawk's settings, in Other.
  • An Animations switch, which also follows Windows' own setting.

Fixes

Windows updates

  • Works again after the updates that changed the system tray and the September taskbar update. (#69, #78, #79, #83, #89, #91)
  • If the button the player sits next to doesn't exist on your build, the player goes to the start of the tray instead of disappearing.
  • The player no longer vanishes when Do Not Disturb is on.

Startup and stability

  • If the player doesn't make it onto the taskbar at startup, the mod tries again. (#67, #68, #73, #82)
  • Media keys keep working after an Explorer restart. (#52)
  • The player corrects itself if it ends up on the wrong side of its tray button.
  • Security report: fixes for callback handling, the shell32 and windhawk.exe lookups, image handling and unloading. (#71)

Which app it follows

  • The player stays on the app that's playing instead of a paused one. (#22)
  • It no longer flashes another app when tracks change. (#34)
  • Ignored apps stay out of session switching, and the ignore list also matches the browser's exe. (#66, #70, #77)

Album art and colors

  • Covers up to 24 MB show up. (#81)
  • Old art no longer stays when a browser track has none. (#33)
  • The Album color works on the progress bar, the visualizer and everything else, including with album art turned off.
  • With no album art, dynamic visualizer colors go back to your normal color. (#58)
  • Solid backgrounds survive switching between light and dark. (#57)

Visualizer

  • Keeps reacting when you switch the player to another app, like Clipchamp, Firefox or Snipping Tool.
  • Much lower GPU use when nothing is playing. (#41)

Monitors

  • Text scrolling and the visualizer keep working after the player moves to another monitor.

Input and placement

  • Pause works reliably in Zen browser. (#26)
  • Right and middle double-click actions fire again.
  • "Hide when no media" no longer keeps taking up space. (#14)
  • Fixed the gap with "Right of Widgets", and the player going under the icons with Taskbar Styler "Borderless". (#74)

Not in this version

  • Showing the player on several monitors at the same time is still planned. (#15, #90)

Thanks

  • Net-zen for the StackPanel tray patch (#87).
  • Everyone who reported bugs and tested the alphas on the Windhawk Discord.

entry.title: Taskbar Thumbnail Stats 1.7
entry.content:
• New "Title at the bottom" option: moves the window name and the close button to a row at the bottom of the thumbnail, closer to the mouse pointer, with configurable top spacing and an optional separator line
  • New "Close button" option: show it only when the mouse is over the thumbnail (Windows default) or always
  • New "Widen small thumbnails to fit the line" option: thumbnails of small windows are made wide enough to show the whole line instead of shortening it with "…"

entry.title: Windows 10 Taskbar Context Menu Fix for Win11 24H2+ 1.3
entry.content: • Fix taskmgr item not working on 26100.1

entry.title: Taskbar Clock to Left 2.3.19
entry.content:
• Support horizontal StackPanel tray layouts alongside Grid.
  • Preserve the clock button's margins when moving it.
  • Use the measured bounds of unfamiliar taskbar buttons to avoid overlap.
  • Retry placement when the clock text size changes. After a width-related fallback, wait for the clock controls or sizing inputs to change before retrying.
  • Track native tray extent, reserved width, and obstacle positions separately when comparing layouts.
  • Use the native clock position when the taskbar item list is missing, and reuse a valid list on routine layout updates.
  • Update the README.

entry.title: MacOS Minimize Animation 3.2.1
entry.content: • Fixed a crash (seen mostly in Firefox) when Windows couldn't allocate the animation's bitmap. If an allocation fails, the animation is now skipped and the window still minimizes, restores or closes normally.

entry.content: • Add a link to Classic Explorerframe for 24H2 and later.
